findings.title: A failed mermaid chunk load is cached for the rest of the session.
findings.body:
`loadMermaid` stores the `import('mermaid')` promise in a module-level variable. If that import rejects once (a transient network error or a chunk-load failure after a deploy), the rejected promise is kept. Every later README with a diagram goes straight to the catch branch and flags all its blocks as errors, until the page is fully reloaded.

Fix: clear the cache when the import rejects, for example `mermaidPromise = import('mermaid').then(m => m.default).catch(e => { mermaidPromise = undefined; throw e; });`.

held.title: The resolution pins mermaid's URL sanitizer to an older version, and nothing explains why.
held.body:
`"mermaid/@braintree/sanitize-url": "7.0.1"` forces the library mermaid uses to sanitize link URLs in diagrams to one fixed version. If mermaid 11.16.0 declares a newer range (I could not see its manifest; recent 11.x releases ask for ^7.1.x), this is a downgrade of a security-relevant dependency. README content is untrusted, so that matters here.

The PR description does not mention the override. Drop it, or justify it and pin to a version inside mermaid's declared range.
